13.0.0.en: Prophets: they either speak of things that will happen in the future, like Agabus, who prophesied that a famine would occur in Jerusalem (ch. 11:28) and about the arrest of Paul there also (ch. 21:10, 11), or they speak about the Kingdom of Heaven, which is the future of our life as believers; that is, they preach and encourage the hearers to prepare for eternal life.

13.0.1.en: With this chapter the acts of the Apostle Paul begin, whereas the first part of the book concentrated on the acts of the Apostle Peter. Here we see the beginning of the work of Paul and Barnabas together on the first journey. The first journey includes the preaching of Paul and Barnabas in Syria, Turkey and Cyprus, traveling by sea and by land.

13.0.2.en: The journey began from Antioch, the first center of the Church of the Gentiles, which was full of many teachers such as Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger (the Black), Lucius of Cyrene (North Africa), Manaen who had been brought up with Herod Antipas the second, the killer of the Baptist, and Paul.

13.1.0.en: Ministered to the Lord: they led the prayers and carried out teaching and visiting of the believers and caring for them in Antioch.

13.1.1.en: Fasted: this shows the importance of fasting and prayer and that they are among the foundations of worship in the early Church. The Holy Ghost said: He declared to the leaders of the Church in some way, whether by an angel or a voice or any other way.

13.1.2.en: During the fasting and prayers of the Church, the Holy Spirit asked for Barnabas and Saul to be set apart for a special ministry of preaching, namely preaching to the Gentiles in many other lands.

13.2.0.en: Fasted… prayed: this shows the importance of joining fasting with prayer in worship, and also as a preparation for any ministry.

13.2.1.en: Laid their hands on them: this shows the importance of the authority of the Church in directing servants to service, for although the ones being sent were Barnabas and Saul, the Apostles who lead the Church, they do not move except by the direction of the council of the Church.

13.2.2.en: The believers fasted and prayed, asking the Lord’s help for them, and laid their hands on them for blessing.

13.2.3.en: The first journey began from Antioch (Syria) by land to Seleucia (Syria), then by sea to Salamis (Cyprus), and after that by land to Paphos (Cyprus), and after that to Perga in Pamphylia (Turkey), then by land to Antioch of Pisidia (Turkey), followed by land to Iconium (Turkey), then by land to Lystra (Turkey), which is the town of the Apostle Timothy, the disciple of Paul, and in which Paul healed the lame man and was stoned. After that he went by land to Derbe (Turkey) and from there to Lystra (Turkey) by land, then also by land to Iconium (Turkey), and after that by land to Antioch of Pisidia (Turkey) and from there to Perga (Turkey) by land, then by land to Attalia (Turkey), and after that by sea to Seleucia (Syria), and finally he returned to Antioch (Syria) by land, where the journey had begun.

13.2.4.en: This journey took the period from A.D. 45 to A.D. 48, and is recorded in chapters (13-14) of this book.

13.2.5.en: Great is the planning of the Holy Spirit, who, if a person entrusts his life to Him, produces great fruit. So seek God’s counsel before any work, and offer many prayers and join them with fasting as much as you can, especially before great undertakings.

13.3.0.en: Being sent forth by the Holy Ghost: a confirmation that God sent them, and that their mission was not of themselves. Seleucia: a port of Antioch on the Orontes River, about 16 miles west of Antioch. Cyprus: an island in the Mediterranean Sea belonging to the Roman Empire, with many Jews in it, which was distinguished by fertility and prosperity at that time; it is present-day Cyprus.

13.3.1.en: The two Apostles came to the island of Cyprus because it was the birthplace of Barnabas (ch. 4:36) and of some of the believers of Antioch, and it is not far from it (about 50 miles), so they began preaching there.

13.4.0.en: Salamis: a city in the southeast of Cyprus and the most important of its commercial ports.

13.4.1.en: As was the custom of the two Apostles, they began proclaiming the good news to the Jews in the synagogue at Salamis, and with them was St. Mark, surnamed John, a disciple to both of them.

13.5.0.en: Gone through the isle: they went from Salamis in the southeast of the island westward toward Paphos, a distance of about 100 miles, knowing that the length of the whole island is 150 miles, so they most likely passed through its towns preaching Christ until they reached Paphos.

13.5.1.en: Paphos: a port in the southwest of the island of Cyprus, famous for the worship of the goddess Venus, and in it was the seat of the Roman authority.

13.5.2.en: Barjesus: the meaning of his name is son of Jesus (Joshua).

13.5.3.en: Paul and Barnabas crossed the island by land to Paphos, where they found a Jew who claimed prophecy and practiced sorcery, whose name was Barjesus.

13.6.0.en: Which was with the deputy: Barjesus was one of the close counselors of the deputy, because Sergius was a lover of knowledge, so he was interested in the prophecies of Barjesus and his sorcery.

13.6.1.en: Called for Barnabas and Saul: when the two Apostles began to preach, the deputy, a lover of knowledge, heard of them, so he wanted to know the new teaching they were preaching.

13.6.2.en: Desired to hear the word of God: regarding it as a new teaching that he wanted to become acquainted with.

13.6.3.en: The deputy Sergius was a man who sought the truth, so he was dazzled by the miracles of that sorcerer even though he was a philosopher and thinker, and when Paul and Barnabas came, he asked them to let him hear their message.

13.7.0.en: Withstood them: by disputation and mockery, relying on the deputy’s confidence in him.

13.7.1.en: Elymas: that is, one of much knowledge; it is an Aramaic name and title of the sorcerer Barjesus and has its meaning in the Arabic language. To turn away the deputy from the faith: the deputy began to be convinced by the preaching of the two Apostles, so the sorcerer tried to confuse his thoughts and cast doubt on him so that he would not believe in Christ.

13.8.0.en: Saul, who is also called Paul: he had two names, and hence his name was called Paul, which is his Latin name, because he had begun preaching to the Gentiles, so it seemed good that his name should be acceptable to them. Set his eyes on him: he looked intently at him in order to judge and punish him and to alert those present to what he would say to him. Here we see Saul (the Hebrew name, meaning “asked for”) and his Latin name Paul (that is, “little”), filled with the Holy Spirit, who supports him in his ministry, and he goes ahead of Barnabas for the first time in acting.

13.9.0.en: All subtilty: the sorcerer relied on deceit to convince his hearers of his words.

13.9.1.en: Child of the devil: because Satan is a liar and the father of lies.

13.9.2.en: Enemy of all righteousness: he resists the word of righteousness that the two Apostles preach and tries to turn people away from faith and godliness.

13.9.3.en: Wilt thou not cease: a rhetorical question to rebuke Elymas for persisting in evil.

13.9.4.en: Paul declared the wickedness and evil of that sorcerer and his opposition to the true work of God.

13.10.0.en: The hand of the Lord is upon thee: God punishes you so that you may repent.

13.10.1.en: For a season: a temporary period, that perhaps he may repent.

13.10.2.en: A mist: his sight became very weak.

13.10.3.en: Darkness: he lost his sight completely.

13.10.4.en: Sought some to lead him by the hand: he was unable to move by himself, that perhaps his feeling of weakness might lead him to repentance and the rejection of pride.

13.10.5.en: Paul asked God that Elymas the sorcerer be struck with blindness for a season until he should repent, so he immediately began to grope in the darkness, deprived of light, just as he wanted to deprive the deputy of the light of faith, and he did not know how to move.

13.11.0.en: Astonished: at the power of the preaching of the two Apostles and the immediate carrying out of the punishment on the greatest of his sorcerers and counselors, being certain of the truth of the new teaching because of its superiority and its evident power over the teaching of the deceiving sorcerer.

13.11.1.en: Truly, what a man sows, that he also reaps. Whoever lights the way of others, God lights his way, and whoever works for their going astray, his own going astray returns upon him. So be concerned to do good and to help those around you, and keep away from condemnation and from any evil, however persuasive it may be or however much the circumstances around you help toward it, and be confident that good is rewarded in the end with very many blessings.

13.12.0.en: Perga in Pamphylia: Pamphylia is a province in the west of Cilicia in present-day Turkey, and the city of Perga is the capital of Pamphylia.

13.12.1.en: The two Apostles moved by sea to the coasts of Turkey, and here St. Mark parted from the two Apostles and returned to Jerusalem and left them. Luke did not mention the reason for the parting, but we learn later that the Apostle Paul was troubled by this, while Barnabas made excuses for him and disagreed with Paul after a while because of what Mark had done (ch. 15:37-39); but the Apostle Paul came back and showed his love and trust in him (2 Tim 4:11).

13.13.0.en: Pisidia: a province lying north of Perga, whose capital is the city of Antioch, which is different from the city of Antioch that lies in Syria, and the road to it from Perga is mountainous and rugged and has many robbers, so the two Apostles were exposed to many dangers, which they endured, trusting in God.

13.13.1.en: Went into the synagogue: in the city of Antioch of Pisidia there was a large number of Jews and of Greeks who had become Jewish proselytes.

13.13.2.en: Sat down: in the place where the teachers sit, since it was customary for Jewish preachers and teachers to pass through the synagogues in different lands and preach in them.

13.13.3.en: Paul and Barnabas and those with them moved on, passing through Perga without preaching in it, and came to Antioch of Pisidia and entered the synagogue to begin preaching in it as was their custom.

13.14.0.en: Men and brethren: it was evident from the appearance and clothing of the two Apostles that they were strangers, but knowledge showed in them, and their sitting in the place of the teachers showed that they were Jews versed in the Holy Scriptures and able to teach.

13.14.1.en: After the reading from the books of Moses and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue asked them to give a word of exhortation if they wished.

13.15.0.en: Then Paul stood up: here Paul continues to go ahead of Barnabas in speaking and preaching, although the latter was known for preaching, but Paul excelled and became famous for it.

13.15.1.en: Beckoning with his hand: that they be silent and pay attention to what he would say.

13.15.2.en: Men of Israel: the Jews, the children of Israel.

13.15.3.en: Ye that fear God: the Greek proselytes who love to hear Jewish teachings and have not yet become Jews. Paul began his first recorded sermon in the Holy Bible, and it closely resembles the sermon of the martyr Stephen, in that it reviews the whole history of the Jewish nation up to the coming of Christ, His crucifixion and His resurrection.

13.16.0.en: Chose our fathers: Paul spoke as a Jew, so he called the fathers “our fathers,” and by the fathers he means Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and his twelve sons.

13.16.1.en: Exalted the people: He blessed them with abundance of offspring and strength.

13.16.2.en: With an high arm: he means the ten plagues and the dividing of the Red Sea.

13.16.3.en: Their manners: their murmurings, their attempts to return to Egypt and their refusal to enter the Promised Land. Paul spoke about God’s choice of Abraham and his offspring, their sojourn in Egypt and their departure from it by the miracles of God, then their journey in the wilderness for forty years, which was full of murmuring.

13.17.0.en: When the children of Israel reached the Promised Land in Canaan, Joshua divided among them the land of seven nations, namely the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, after destroying these peoples. The land of Canaan was the lowland west of the Jordan, and the land of Aram is the highland east of the Jordan.

13.18.0.en: The children of Israel did not drive out all the wicked inhabitants of the land, being lax in carrying out Joshua’s commandments, so they rose against them and occupied them and humbled them, and they cried out to God, who sent them judges who delivered them, and this was in what is called the age of the Judges, which lasted 450 years, and the last of these judges was Samuel the prophet.

13.19.0.en: The children of Israel asked Samuel to choose a king for them, so he was angry and rebuked them because God is their King, but God agreed in order to satisfy them, and gave them Saul the Benjamite, whom they had asked for, and he ruled them for 40 years.

13.20.0.en: God rejected King Saul because of his evil, and anointed David as king by the hand of Samuel. David was obedient to God and his heart was pure like His, and he walked according to His will.

13.21.0.en: God promised to raise up a Savior from the seed of David, and He fulfilled this, giving to His people Israel Jesus Christ as Savior (2 Sam 7:12, 13, 16; Ps 89:36-37). This verse is the goal of the sermon of the Apostle Paul, and what precedes it is a preparation for it.

13.22.0.en: Fulfilled his course: he completes his ministry and his preaching after baptizing people unto repentance.

13.22.1.en: John the Baptist, known among all the Jews for his greatness and the truth of his words, prepared for the coming of Jesus Christ with the baptism of repentance, confessing his weakness before the great Christ who was coming after him.

13.23.0.en: Brethren: a gentle expression of love toward the Jewish hearers that draws them to faith.

13.23.1.en: Children of the stock of Abraham: the Jews who take pride in their sonship to Abraham.

13.23.2.en: Whosoever among you feareth God: he means the Greek proselytes who love to hear Jewish teachings, that is, the Gentiles who love God.

13.23.3.en: The word of this salvation: the preaching of Christ the Savior.

13.23.4.en: Paul began gently inviting his hearers, Jews and Gentiles, to accept faith in Christ the Savior.

13.24.0.en: Knew him not: they did not understand that Jesus is the awaited Messiah, because they supposed that the Messiah was an earthly king and not a spiritual one.

13.24.1.en: The voices of the prophets: which show that the Messiah would suffer and die for His people.

13.24.2.en: Condemned him: that He deserved death.

13.24.3.en: The Jews who dwell in Jerusalem, where the Temple is, rejected faith in Jesus Christ and persecuted Him, and even condemned Him to death, and thus they fulfilled the prophecies of the prophets.

13.25.0.en: The Jews of Jerusalem tried to catch any fault in Christ throughout His life and did not find any, and His righteousness and innocence were proved; yet, in their wickedness, they asked Pilate the governor to kill Him.

13.26.0.en: The tree: the Cross. After the chief priests completed the agreement with Judas, the disciple of Christ, to betray Him, they seized Him and struck Him and mocked Him and crucified Him until He died and was buried in the tomb.

13.27.0.en: The Jews thought they had gotten rid of Christ, but they were surprised by His resurrection on the third day. He said: “God raised him,” meaning by that that the Father by His will and the Son by His divinity raised His body from death on the third day.

13.28.1.en: Them which came up with him from Galilee: the twelve and the Apostles and many of His disciples and followers. Christ confirmed His resurrection by appearing many times during forty days after His resurrection to His disciples, who preach in His name and bear witness to His resurrection.

13.29.0.en: The promise: God’s promise to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and all the fathers of the Jewish nation of the awaited Messiah.

13.29.1.en: As the Apostles preached in Jerusalem and Judea, so Paul and Barnabas now preach in Antioch of Pisidia to fulfill God’s promise of salvation for the whole world in Christ Jesus.

13.30.0.en: Paul cited the second Psalm, which spoke of the divinity of Christ, and that He is the eternal Son of God who was born as an incarnate man at a specific time to save the world; this God has fulfilled for us in these days by the redemption of Christ, His death and His resurrection.

13.31.0.en: No more to return to corruption: He does not die again like those raised from the dead, such as Lazarus, the daughter of Jairus and the son of the widow of Nain.

13.31.1.en: The sure mercies of David: God’s promises to David of the salvation that is accomplished in Christ and that we receive in the Church of the New Testament.

13.31.2.en: Christ rose from the dead with a resurrection after which there is no death, to give human beings the enjoyment of the mercies of Christ, the Son of David.

13.32.0.en: David mentioned in (Ps 16:10) that His body, that is, the body of Christ, would not see corruption, and of course this is about Christ and not about David, who died and was buried with his fathers and whose body decayed after he had completed his service as king; but Christ is the One who rose and saw no corruption.

13.33.0.en: Be it known unto you: to show the importance of the following words.

13.33.2.en: The law of Moses: it shows sin and its punishment and the reward of carrying out the commandment, but it is unable to justify man; the One who justifies us is Christ alone, by His blood.

13.33.3.en: This is the message of forgiveness, that is, escape from punishment, and of justification, that is, innocence and deliverance from evil. Thus through Him we escape from the daily dominion of sin and from its eternal punishment, which the Law was unable to grant us.

13.34.0.en: Ye despisers: those who refuse to obey the word of God, whether in the days of Habakkuk or at the preaching of Christ.

13.34.1.en: Wonder: you do not believe and understand.

13.34.2.en: Perish: the coming of divine punishment upon the Jews in the days of Habakkuk, or the killing of the Jews in Jerusalem in A.D. 70. A work in your days: the destruction that comes upon those who reject faith.

13.34.3.en: A work which ye shall in no wise believe, though a man declare it unto you: a terrible destruction for those who reject the word of God, whether by the Babylonian captivity in the days of Habakkuk or the destruction by the demolition of the Temple and Jerusalem in A.D. 70, and all this is a warning of the terrible torment in the eternal fire.

13.34.4.en: The Apostle Paul warned them against treating the message lightly, lest there be fulfilled in them the saying of the prophets in “Hab 1:5” about those who are lax in their life with God, so the Babylonian captivity came upon them as a discipline for them, and unfortunately they did not believe his prophecy until they actually perished at the hands of the Babylonians. We note that twenty years after this sermon, destruction and ruin came upon Jerusalem at the hands of the Romans.

13.34.5.en: This is the message of salvation offered to us for our benefit.

13.34.6.en: God is calling you to repent, so do not reject His voice sent to you in the Holy Bible and on the lips of the Fathers and teachers in the Church. The opportunity of repentance is available now so that you may enjoy His forgiveness, and He will even pour out His grace upon you and rescue you from eternal destruction.

13.35.s.en: (4) The opposition to Paul in Antioch of Pisidia

13.35.0.en: After the end of the sermon, the hearers were moved, especially the Gentiles, that is, the devout Greeks who love to attend the synagogues of the Jews and listen to the sermons but had not yet become Jews, and they expressed their longing for the new teaching by asking the two Apostles to complete their teaching on the coming Sabbath, which is the time of the weekly meeting in the synagogue.

13.36.0.en: The religious proselytes: the Greeks who love to hear Jewish teachings in the synagogue. The hearers who admired the words of the two Apostles did not wait for the coming Sabbath to hear about Christ, but followed the two Apostles, and those who followed were not only Gentiles but also Jews, and they used to go to them in the house where they stayed to hear their teachings; and the two Apostles seized these opportunities and went on confirming their faith in Christ, which had begun within them.

13.37.0.en: Almost the whole city: not only the Jews but also the pagan Gentiles, for most of the city’s inhabitants were pagans.

13.37.1.en: Envy: since they felt that the Jewish teachings had not attracted the pagans as the new teaching did, and because they regard the Jews as distinct from the Gentiles, how could they now be equal in the Christian faith. Spake against: they present arguments against the new teaching to cast doubt on it.

13.37.2.en: Contradicting: declaring that the right teaching is the Jewish one and showing the error of the new teaching. Blaspheming: declaring that the awaited Messiah is not the weak Jesus who suffered and died. When very many people gathered at the synagogue on the following Sabbath, the Jews were jealous of the success of the two Apostles, and began to oppose them and to blaspheme against the preaching.

13.38.0.en: Waxed bold: he was not afraid but declared the right teaching and the danger to the Jews in their opposing it.

13.38.1.en: It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: it is God’s will that the Jews be preached to first about Christ, because they are the people of God who know the prophecies and are awaiting the Messiah, so they would have a greater readiness for faith.

13.38.2.en: Put it from you: you rejected faith.

13.38.3.en: Unworthy of everlasting life: you will receive the punishment of rejecting faith, which is eternal torment. We turn to the Gentiles: the focus on preaching to the Gentiles.

13.38.4.en: A light of the Gentiles: Christ is the light of the whole world, and His Apostles and servants preach Him to the Gentiles and bring them out of the darkness of sin into the light of faith.

13.38.5.en: For salvation unto the ends of the earth: the salvation of Christ is offered to the whole world and not only to the Jews.

13.38.6.en: The two Apostles confronted them with the fact that their rejection of the word of God confirms their unworthiness of it, and that they would preach to the Gentiles according to the prophecy of Isaiah the prophet (Isa 49:6) on the right of the Gentiles to salvation.

13.39.0.en: That: that is, salvation is offered to the Gentiles as to the Jews.

13.39.1.en: Glorified the word of the Lord: they held fast to the faith and thanked God.

13.39.2.en: The Gentiles rejoiced greatly and many believed who were known to God by His foreknowledge and who have a share in eternal life, and the word of the Lord spread in the region.

13.40.0.en: Stirred up: they spoke against the two Apostles and showed the error of their teachings, and stirred up the women and the rulers of the city against them.

13.40.1.en: Devout women: those of pagan origin who were interested in attending the synagogue of the Jews and hearing its teachings, whether they had become Jewesses or were still pagans and only loved to hear Jewish teachings. Honourable: the rich who held a high position in society.

13.40.2.en: The chief men of the city: the great and elder men of the city who influence the leadership of society, and they are probably relatives or acquaintances of the honorable women, so they were influenced by their words.

13.40.3.en: Persecution: in the form of rebuke and mockery.

13.40.4.en: Expelled them: they drove them out of the city with contempt.

13.40.5.en: The Jews pushed forward some of the Gentile women who had standing in society, and they stirred up a persecution against the two Apostles and drove them out of the city.

13.41.0.en: Against them: a testimony against the Jews who drove them out that they reject faith.

13.41.1.en: Iconium: a city in Asia Minor southeast of Antioch of Pisidia, 50 miles away from Antioch.

13.41.2.en: The two Apostles fulfilled the commandment of Christ to shake off the dust of their feet against the city (Lk 9:5), declaring that they sought no personal benefit from the preaching, so they took nothing from the city, not even the dust of the ground, then they came to Iconium also in Turkey.

13.42.0.en: The disciples: those who believed in Christ and became His disciples, since the Christians were called disciples.

13.42.1.en: The new believers were exceedingly joyful in the faith and in the work of the Holy Spirit despite the tribulation and persecution.

13.42.2.en: Our Christianity is able to gladden our hearts whatever troubles we find in the world.

13.42.3.en: Let us hold fast to God’s commandments even if others oppose us, and offer our love and our service to all without ceasing, for in the end they win hearts.

13.42.4.en: The rest of the first journey
